sources.entry: SpreadPaper - Spread a single high-resolution wallpaper across multiple monitors, with compensation for the bezel gaps between displays.

summary.one_liner: SpreadPaper is a free, open-source native macOS app that spreads one high-resolution image as a wallpaper across multiple monitors, with bezel compensation for the gaps between displays.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you use a single image as a wallpaper spanning all connected displays, positioned by dragging on a canvas that mirrors your macOS display arrangement. Supports three kinds of wallpaper: Static (one image), Light & Dark (two images switched by macOS appearance), and Dynamic (up to 16 images on a time-of-day schedule). The editor offers zoom, fit and flip controls, drag and drop import, and a preview before saving. Bezel compensation lets you set each monitor's frame width so the image lines up across the gaps when there are two or more displays. A library holds saved presets that can be reapplied, duplicated, renamed, filtered and searched, and Settings checks for new releases.
use_cases: Spread a panoramic photo across several monitors
Set a different wallpaper for light and dark mode on macOS
Create a wallpaper that changes through the day
Line up a wallpaper across monitor bezels
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
Build and run in Xcode with ⌘R
Alternatively, download SpreadPaper.dmg or .zip from the Releases page and move the app to Applications
notable: Bezel compensation for monitor frame gaps
Light & Dark and time-of-day Dynamic wallpaper modes
Canvas that syncs with the macOS display arrangement
Presets saved in a gallery with one-click reapply
Universal build for Intel and Apple silicon
caveats: Not signed with a paid Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper warns on first launch and needs a manual override
On macOS 15 and later, Control-click to open no longer bypasses the warning
